subject: Dedicated GPU pool — sizing & pricing after your load test
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@luminahealth.com, cto@luminahealth.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — sizing & pricing after your load test

Hi Emma / Raj,

Thanks again for sharing the preliminary load test artifacts. I pulled the traces and the CSV you provided (attached) and ran a quick pass with our infra team to map your observed TPS/latency to Dedicated sizing options. High level summary up front so procurement has something to act on:

- Short prompts (avg token length ~45): observed ~420 requests/sec at peak in your test harness, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~470ms (spikey).
- Longer context/LL prompt mixes reduced throughput: sustained ~110–140 req/sec with p95 ~210ms.
- Your tracepack shows hot KV cache misses on some session patterns which explains the p99 spikes.

Attached: "lumina-loadtest-tps-20270512.csv" (raw TPS by run), "trace-heap-20270512.json" (sampled traces).

Next steps I recommend:
1) A Dedicated pool sized to cover your 95th percentile sustained throughput: our analysis suggests a 6-GPU A100-equivalent pool configured with conservative batching (batch cap 32) will cover your mixed workload with headroom for autoscaling bursts.
2) Commit options to discuss: 12-month reserved commit (preferred) vs 24-month for deeper discounts.
3) SLA / Latency guarantees: we can offer a p95 latency SLO as part of the commit; p99 recovery will depend on KV cache tuning and client-side session affinity.

Rishi and Sergio are cc'd — they'll follow up with pricing bands and configuration recommendations. If you can confirm target committed term (12 vs 24 months) and expected annualized usage (e.g., avg rps during business hours), we'll produce a formal proposal.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: lumina-loadtest-tps-20270512.csv, trace-heap-20270512.json

From: procurement@luminahealth.com <procurement@luminahealth.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — sizing & pricing after your load test

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick read. A few clarifications from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement needs a pricing anchor for a 12-month committed spend. We will likely target a 12-month fixed commit to start; open to 24-month if the delta is >15% annual savings.
- Engineering (Raj, cc'd) flagged the p99 spikes — their expectation is p95 < 150ms during business hours for the short-prompt flows. p99 can be higher but we need visibility into mitigation (cache warm-up, routing).
- Can Redwood provide an option to reserve extra burst capacity (on top of the commit) for peak events at a clearly defined purchase price? We may want 30–50% burstability for quarterly demo days.

Also attaching the internal test harness notes (see attached traces). Can you confirm whether your 6-GPU recommendation assumes KV cache enabled and session-affinity?

Procurement asks for: an initial committed pricing sheet, clear notes on what constitutes the committed unit (GPU-hours vs throughput SLA), and any termination / ramp clauses.

Best,
Emma Liu
Procurement Manager, Lumina Health
procurement@luminahealth.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — sizing & pricing after your load test

Emma / Raj / Vivek / Rishi —

I dug into the raw runs and simulated capacity using our serving model. Key notes and the concrete options below. I attached the per-run CSV exported from our bench harness (lumina-loadtest-tps-20270512.csv).

Technical assumptions:
- Baseline model: open-llama-13B-v2 optimized; A100-equivalent perf numbers used (we can switch to V100/T4 mixes if needed).
- KV cache enabled with session affinity improves effective throughput by ~28% for your short-prompt profile (we measured cache hit ~62% across sampled runs).
- Batch cap 32, concurrency per GPU tuned to keep p95 < 150ms in steady state.

Sizing options (expected sustained throughput / p95 estimates):
A) 4x A100-equiv pool (conservative batching) — Sustained 220–260 req/s, p95 ~140ms for short prompts, p99 ~380–450ms on cold sessions. Good for smaller pilots.
B) 6x A100-equiv pool (recommended for production) — Sustained 320–420 req/s, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~300–360ms with KV tuning. Handles mixed short and long context workloads with headroom.
C) 8x A100-equiv pool (high-availability) — Sustained 420–520 req/s, p95 ~100–120ms, p99 ~200–280ms. Suitable if you need burst-for-demo margin and lower p99.

Notes on burst capacity: our Dedicated product supports configured burst capacity as an additive percentage of commit (e.g., +30%). Burst instances are billed at a higher overage rate and are pre-warmed for demo events if scheduled 48h in advance to avoid cold p99s.

Pricing mapping (very rough for now, formal quote to follow):
- Per-GPU effective monthly cost used: $7,200 / GPU (on a 12-month commit baseline) — this maps to our reserved pricing bands.
- Using that baseline: 6x pool monthly committed cost ~ $43k/month. 24-month commits reduce per-GPU to ~$6,000 (approx 17% savings).

I'll push a formal PDF with exact numbers and a few alternative commit tiers. Rishi — want me to include the pilot/discovery package numbers (30-day reduced rate) in the proposal?

Sergio
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachments: lumina-loadtest-tps-20270512.csv, trace-heap-20270512.json

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@luminahealth.com, cto@luminahealth.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated — proposal (v3) and commit options

Emma / Raj —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood Dedicated proposal v3 (redwood-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf) which contains three committed options and our standard SLA language. Highlights:

- Option 1 (Pilot): 4x GPU committed for 3 months — $32,000/month, no long-term commitment; ideal for ramp validation.
- Option 2 (Production): 6x GPU committed for 12 months — $43,200/month; includes p95 latency SLO (business hours), 1 scheduled burst day per quarter (up to +30% capacity) at a predetermined burst rate.
- Option 3 (Enterprise): 6x GPU committed for 24 months — $36,000/month effective; includes upgraded support, 48h pre-warm for burst events, and a 3% monthly overage credit if p95 SLO missed more than twice in a quarter.

Discounting and flexibility:
- We can offer a one-time 5% sign-up credit for a DocuSign within 14 days.
- We will consider deeper discounts (7–12%) for a 36-month commitment or a higher committed GPU count (>12 GPUs).

Definitions you asked for:
- Committed unit: guaranteed GPU-hours per month equivalent (e.g., 6 GPUs * hours) and an associated throughput SLO (we map GPU-hours to expected sustained TPS in the proposal appendix).
- Termination: standard 90-day notice for down-scaling after month 6; early termination fees apply based on remaining committed GPU-hours.

Next steps: confirm which option (Pilot vs Production vs Enterprise). If you want the Production option with an additional burst buffer (Emma's request for 30–50%), we can append a burst addendum with explicit overage pricing.

I'll leave it to Vivek and Sergio for any technical appendix clarifications.

Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf

From: Rajesh Kumar <cto@luminahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Liu <procurement@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — proposal (v3) and commit options

Rishi / Vivek / Sergio —

Appreciate the clear proposal. Lumina is prepared to sign the 12-month Production option (6x GPUs) subject to one amendment: we need a contracted burst buffer of +20% baseline capacity available on-demand (not just scheduled), billed at a predictable overage rate (proposed: 1.5x of committed unit price per GPU-hour). Our legal team has limited appetite for variable burst pricing during demos — predictable economics are a must.

Two follow-ups:
1) Please send a redline showing the burst addendum and the impact on monthly effective pricing.
2) We want a short pilot window (30 days) post-signature to validate p95 <150ms on our production traffic patterns; if the pilot fails due to performance, Lumina can exit with no further commitment.

If those two items are ok, we will route to procurement and should be able to return an approved DocuSign within 10 business days.

Regards,
Rajesh Kumar
CTO, Lumina Health
cto@luminahealth.com
